abstract_sentences.text: Auto-bidding is a critical tool for advertisers to improve advertising performance.

Recent progress has demonstrated that AI-Generated Bidding (AIGB), which learns a conditional generative planner from offline data, achieves superior performance compared to typical offline reinforcement learning (RL)-based auto-bidding methods.

evidence.anchor: conditional generative planner from offline data

abstract_sentences.text: However, existing AIGB methods still face a performance bottleneck due to their inherent inability to explore beyond the static dataset with feedback.

evidence.anchor: inability to explore beyond the static dataset

abstract_sentences.text: To address this, we propose AIGB-Pearl (Planning with EvaluAtor via RL), a novel method that integrates generative planning and policy optimization.

evidence.anchor: integrates generative planning and policy optimization

abstract_sentences.text: The core of AIGB-Pearl lies in constructing a trajectory evaluator to assess the quality of generated scores and designing a provably sound KL-Lipschitz-constrained score-maximization scheme to ensure safe and efficient exploration beyond the offline dataset.
A practical algorithm that incorporates the synchronous coupling technique is further developed to ensure the model regularity required by the proposed scheme.
Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world advertising systems demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our approach.

statistical_analysis.aggregation_unit: Advertiser aggregate over an A/B day window for real experiments; simulated budget cell or policy mixture for simulated experiments; evaluator metrics aggregate trajectory/pair samples.
statistical_analysis.center_and_dispersion: Main Tables 1–4 and 8/11–13 report point values and relative deltas; Table 5 reports values with ± on OOD; Figures 10–13 show 10 seed curves.
statistical_analysis.uncertainty: No confidence interval, hypothesis test, multiple-comparison correction, bootstrap, Bayesian analysis, regression or effect-size calculation is reported. The meaning of Table 5 ± is not specified.
statistical_analysis.decision_quantities: GMV, BuyCnt, ROI, Cost, relative delta, MAE, AUC, SMAPE, Lipschitz constants, Online Rate, Bad Case Rate and Cost Rate.
statistical_analysis.practical_threshold: Cost within ±2% is the stated acceptable tolerance; Appendix F.4 pathology thresholds are >10% single-step cost, >40% first/last 24-step cost, or total cost <90%.
statistical_analysis.mechanism_vs_significance: Constraint ablation and Lipschitz plots provide mechanism-direction evidence, while statistical significance and replicate uncertainty remain unreported.
statistical_analysis.caption_sufficiency: Tables state units, horizons and metric direction for most comparisons; Figure 10–13 captions identify 10 seeds but do not provide aggregate definitions or dispersion summaries.

final_judgment.single_storyline: AIGB-Pearl adds a supervised trajectory evaluator to AIGB, bounds evaluator bias with Wasserstein/KL/Lipschitz arguments, and trains a planner with score maximization plus shared-noise coupling for constrained extrapolation beyond y_m.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Task formalization, AIGB gap, evaluator/planner mechanism, Theorems 1–3 statements, Eq. (8)–(13), RQ(1)–(4), main tables, constraint ablation, Lipschitz diagnostics and train/OOD evaluator accuracy.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: DDPM details, full proofs, Algorithm 1, hardware/settings, TargetROAS, 10-seed stability, multi-modal data, evaluator loss ablations, KL tuning, first-price extension, online-scope discussion and LLM-usage statement.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Eq. (5) bias gap → Eq. (6)/(7) two controllable W1 terms → Eq. (8) constrained target → Eq. (9)/(10) bound/tuning → Eq. (11)–(13) trainable losses; Figures 1–2 and Table 4 reinforce the chain.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Theorem-bound tightness and joint parameter effects are not measured; synchronous versus random coupling lacks a matched ablation; real A/B tables are mostly point aggregates without traffic/randomization/split or per-advertiser uncertainty; extensions are scattered across the appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For offline generative decision methods, order the paper as feedback/error source → certifiable distance or regularizer → trainable surrogate → matched mechanism ablation → operational failure criterion, and pair each safety/stability claim with a process measure or replicate statistic.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits settings with observable trajectory quality, estimable distribution distance and operational constraints. When reward is unobservable or online interaction is restricted to a separate safe-exploration policy, narrow theorem and safety language to the measured data range and mark the rest open.
